key_insight: The paper shows that recovering constitutive forces from noisy Allen-Cahn image sequences requires noise-aware moment equations before inversion, not just a stronger optimizer or more flexible regularization.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable force inference from microscopy-like movies, improving prediction of unseen planar and 3D interface dynamics for diffuse-interface models.
method: Derive observation-aware, noise-adjusted moment equations to correct bias from nonlinear measurement noise and shared noise coupling.
Invert the corrected moments with a surface-tension-calibrated constitutive transformer (SCCT) using a positive Bernstein basis.
Adapt prior and precision from images and moments, with a conditional stability bound linking moment residuals to prior error.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests and a ring-cage breakup case show that correcting the estimating equation has the largest benefit, and the inferred forces can predict unseen planar and three-dimensional evolutions.
watch_item: The learned adaptation gain is smaller and comparison-dependent, so implementation should prioritize unbiased moment correction and check diffuse-interface accuracy even when topology matches.
paper_title: Inferring constitutive forces from noisy Allen-Cahn movies with moment equations
